summary: Imagine you’re an astronaut who just landed on the Jezero Crater region looking to explore evidence of water from long ago. But, the problem is you don’t know where to start! That’s why I created Jezero Exploration. This map shows you water areas all across the region. Exploration, however, comes at a risk. You don't know the dangers out there that could determine your life. This map includes radiation, a big risk factor that damages the body. It also includes dust, pressure, and temperature, so that you can explore with confidence. Exploring uncertain regions also means that you have to navigate your way to certain places. That’s where the JezeroNav comes in. It helps you choose different routes, so you can find your way in the Jezero area. Astronauts using the Jezero Exploration tool will allow them to safely discover new scientific findings.
details:
Jezero Explorer is a web-based tool designed to help future astronauts explore Mars more safely and efficiently. It combines data from NASA missions to create an interactive view of the Martian terrain and environment.

The project uses Python to analyze NASA datasets and convert them into JSON files and visual images that the website can read. This Python processing is performed only once during the data preparation stage. Once the data has been processed and exported, the website can reuse the generated files without having to run the Python analysis again every time someone visits. This makes the application more efficient and reduces the amount of processing required by the website.

For terrain data, Python processes GeoTIFF files and extracts elevation information. The website then uses JavaScript to display the processed data and visualize the terrain.

The tool also analyzes environmental measurements, including temperature, dust, radiation, and atmospheric pressure, over the period from November 11–18. I used NumPy to help analyze the environmental and radiation data, and Pillow to process the TIFF images. The processed information is exported into JSON files so the website can access and display it.

Astronauts can select a destination and use the tool to view the surrounding terrain, elevation, and environmental information. It also calculates a route, showing the shortest distance and estimated travel time to reach the selected destination. This helps astronauts understand the terrain ahead and make more informed decisions when planning an exploration.

For the website, I used React to build the interface, Vite for the development configuration, and Tailwind CSS for styling. I also used React Three Fiber to create the 3D terrain visualization. Codex helped me with coding, debugging, and developing ideas throughout the project.

The main goal of Jezero Explorer is to bring different types of NASA data together in one place, with astronaut safety as the main priority. By combining terrain visualization, route planning, and environmental information, the project aims to help future Mars explorers plan their missions while identifying potential risks and interesting scientific areas.
